incident-bot: [PAGER] SEV=high -> auth.errors > 50/min (customer: Garnet Private VPC). Auto-joined channel. Alert: https://alerts.redwood.internal/alerts/INC-2475012345 :thumbsdown:

sylvie: I'm oncall for infra today, taking this. starting triage now — first look at counts and zones.

sylvie: quick note: spike started ~2026-08-12T07:12:00Z. Errors are 401 from tenant-bridge -> auth-proxy. Affected region: eu-west-1 (Garnet dedicated pool). No other customers flagged so far.

garnet-oncall: Confirmed from our side, ~20% of API calls failing to auth in eu-west-1 for the last 8m. Login flows returning 401 for a subset of clients. No DB errors.

tia (oncall): tagging SRE: @omar @taylor-sre. Can we get logs for auth-proxy and envoy? Any recent config or cert rotates?

omar: pulling logs from one symptomatic proxy pod now.

omar: relevant tail of proxy log:```
2026-08-12T07:14:12Z auth-proxy[2142]: WARN tls: handshake error from 10.2.8.14: remote error: tls: bad certificate
2026-08-12T07:14:12Z auth-proxy[2142]: WARN ssl: session resumed with unknown cert-id
2026-08-12T07:14:13Z auth-proxy[2142]: ERROR oauth: token validation failed: jwks lookup failed: 401 upstream
```

benji: we did rotate the tenant CA bundle earlier today (09:30 local) as part of scheduled rotation for Garnet. My change posted a new CA into the keystore and removed the old CA from the active list. Hypothesis: TCP session / TLS session resumption is sticking to old backends that still trust the earlier CA or have stale SSL session tickets. Envoy/ALB session cache might be reusing a session that no longer validates after CA removal.

sylvie: that matches. I see connection reuse count high on the LB in metrics. Quick mitigation options: 1) drain and restart auth-proxy pods to clear session cache; 2) set envoy transport_socket to disable session ticket/resumption for a short window; 3) re-add old CA temporarily (less ideal). Which is fastest?

taylor-sre: restart auth-proxy pods is lowest blast radius and quick. We'll do rolling restart across the Garnet dedicated pool to clear TLS session caches. Prep: backing out only if traffic doesn't recover.

benji: noted. be sure to cordon the node or set pod PDBs appropriately; we have capacity to take 1/3 down.

sylvie: executing rolling restart now. command:```bash
kubectl -n private-garnet rollout restart deploy/auth-proxy -l shard=garnet-eu
kubectl -n private-garnet get pods -l app=auth-proxy -w
```

sylvie: first batch restarted. Logs show no more "bad certificate" on new pods, envoy reports new TLS handshakes.

garnet-oncall: after first batch - error rate dropped from 20% -> 5%. Some clients still hit old SLB sessions.

omar: we can also forcibly clear envoys' SSL session cache with admin endpoint:```bash
# on each envoy admin port
curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:9901/clear_tls_sessions
```
I pushed that to the remaining pods, results look good. Metrics: auth.errors ~0.6% now.

tia (oncall): customer impact update: Garnet says degraded auth for ~15 minutes, critical flows for internal ops affected; they accepted a 10-minute maintenance window.

benji: following up — we will roll back the CA purge step in the rotation job as a safety net, re-add old CA to keystore for 1 hour to allow any stale sessions to drain, then re-run rotation with a 1-minute grace where we restart the proxies first. Creating a short-run scheduled task.

taylor-sre: post-mitigations: add runbook step to restart auth-proxy before removing old CA, and add a proactive check in rotation CI to perform a handshake test using persisted session tickets. Also add an alert for "envoy ssl session reuse after CA change" (heuristic: spike in tls: bad certificate + migration window).

sylvie: summary for incident log for customer comms: cause = CA rotation + TLS session resumption + session cache not cleared -> intermittent 401s for Garnet private pool in eu-west-1. Mitigation = rolling restart of auth-proxy + clear envoy tls sessions + temporary re-add of old CA. Status = stable, residual error ~0.2% (within SLO).

garnet-oncall: confirmed we see normal auth behavior across our test clients now. Thanks team for fast response. We'll coordinate a follow-up maintenance to tidy keystore.

sylvie: creating follow-up tickets:
- TICKET-1182: update rotation job to restart proxies before CA removal
- TICKET-1183: add envoy clear_tls_sessions step to rotation runbook
- TICKET-1184: synthetic test for CA rotation session-resumption case

sylvie: marking incident as mitigated. Will run full postmortem with timeline and RCA tomorrow. cc: @product-security for advisory.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2475012345 marked MITIGATED by sylvie. Postmortem scheduled: 2026-08-13T15:00:00Z.

sylvie: quick nits: please add the exact kube commands and admin endpoints used into the runbook notes — I pasted them above. Also we should add customer-facing note template for "certificate rotation caused short auth disruption, mitigated by restarting auth-proxy and re-adding old CA temporarily".

benji: will draft customer note and share in #customer-success. :white_check_mark: 

taylor-sre: follow-ups assigned. closing channel unless Garnet reopens. :wave:
